previous_action: Gaius Maximus Valerius organizes regular patrols of the road and sends dispatches across the Roman world seeking skilled shipwrights and sailors for a private commercial fleet operating under Roman law. He begins collecting profits from the road and port, stores wealth separately between the main estate and port, and establishes public and private wealth accounts with a fixed 10% transfer of realized net public profit into the private account.

continuity.campaign_development: Valerius's road is now regularly patrolled, the lake port is producing recurring commercial receipts, and commercial reserves are decentralized between the main estate and port. A separate private household reserve has been established. The public commercial account retains 90% of each realized net profit for operations and reinvestment, while 10% moves to the private reserve without automatic compounding. Dispatches are seeking shipwrights and sailors for a modest private commercial fleet; no naval command or public authority has been claimed.
